question: When someone says they like every kind of music except one, what does the exception tend to reveal?
answer: A class line. Bethany Bryson analysed 1993 US survey data: better-educated people disliked fewer genres, but the ones they did reject, chiefly gospel, country, rap and heavy metal, were those whose fans had the least schooling. Their open-mindedness had a border, and it ran along the people below them.
move: Notice whom a tolerant boast leaves out; that edge is the real rule.
ask: When I say I like everything except one thing, whose world am I quietly leaving out?
reference: Bryson, Anything but heavy metal: symbolic exclusion and musical dislikes, American Sociological Review, 1996
